bug_semantics: When an application evaluates attacker-controlled JSONata expressions, an attacker can call $toMillis with a crafted non-matching timestamp and no picture argument. The default path runs iso8601regex.test(timestamp); the original regex used repeated optional date/time groups with * quantifiers, so a long near-match can force superlinear backtracking before rejection and exhaust CPU.
flaw_origin: Commit c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 first added both the vulnerable ISO-8601 regular expression and the default-picture $toMillis branch that tests untrusted timestamp text against it in src/datetime.js. Its immediate parent 5e65aff620167854810cde88c2a2580403d9eb38 has neither iso8601regex nor the toMillis function. The all-ref reverse -S history identifies c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 as the first surviving writer; it is a one-parent commit with no finer public member history to decompose.
ai_marker: absent: BIC author is andrew-coleman <andrew_coleman@uk.ibm.com>, committer is Matt Bailey <mattbaileyuk@users.noreply.github.com>, and the complete commit message has only Signed-off-by: andrew-coleman <andrew_coleman@uk.ibm.com>; no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker appears in the commit object
evidence: The assigned GHSA bundle states that malicious non-matching $toMillis inputs cause superlinear backtracking in the ISO-8601 validation regex, identifies affected ranges >=2.0.0,<2.2.0 and <1.8.9, and names patched versions 2.2.0 and 1.8.9.

CVE.org API record CVE-2026-52746 was PUBLISHED when checked and independently describes the same $toMillis superlinear-backtracking denial of service, the same affected ranges, and fixes in 2.2.0 and 1.8.9; it is not rejected or withdrawn.

git show c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 -- src/datetime.js shows that commit adding iso8601regex with (-[01]\d)*, (-[0-3]\d)*, and (T...)* plus toMillis(timestamp, picture), whose no-picture branch calls iso8601regex.test(timestamp).
git show 5e65aff620167854810cde88c2a2580403d9eb38:src/datetime.js followed by searches for iso8601regex and function toMillis finds neither, directly verifying immediate-parent absence.

git log --all --reverse -S of the vulnerable regex in src/datetime.js returns c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 as its first addition, d6ffc17cb16a8e53c222205bd274624e919cce0b as the mainline removal, and f659e42c24e680f61b3c449dc0415b918a020869 as the v1 backport removal.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 shows c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 has the single parent 5e65aff620167854810cde88c2a2580403d9eb38; the full commit object contains no squash-member list or AI-authorship trailer.

git tag --contains c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 starts at v1.6.0 and includes v1.8.8 and all inspected v2 releases; v1.5.4 lacks iso8601regex/toMillis, establishing the vulnerable feature's release boundary rather than treating older function-absent tags as vulnerable code.

git show d6ffc17cb16a8e53c222205bd274624e919cce0b -- src/datetime.js shows the direct mainline fix changing all three repeated ISO-8601 component groups from * to ?, eliminating the repeated optional groups responsible for the backtracking mechanism.

git merge-base --is-ancestor verifies d6ffc17cb16a8e53c222205bd274624e919cce0b is in v2.2.0 but not v2.1.1; the equivalent v1 backport f659e42c24e680f61b3c449dc0415b918a020869 is in v1.8.9 but not v1.8.8.

GitHub PR 793 is merged to master with merge_commit_sha d6ffc17cb16a8e53c222205bd274624e919cce0b and title 'fix iso8601 regex pattern'; advisory-listed commit 80ba95d170f74e3f20f4f36b8b77d8c85cea7686 instead fixes fractional-second parsing and is not the direct regex-complexity fix.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is source-to-sink complete: c1721bfacb9a13833248309aa31fe3478b04bc41 introduced the permissive repeated-group ISO-8601 regex and immediately exposed it through the no-picture $toMillis validation path; crafted attacker-controlled near-matches can consume CPU during regex rejection. The exact lines are absent from its verified immediate parent, and bounded all-ref pickaxe history finds no earlier writer or reconstructable member commit, so this surviving one-parent object is the atomic public BIC despite touching other files. The BIC is present from v1.6.0 and precedes the affected v1 and v2 release lines. d6ffc17cb16a8e53c222205bd274624e919cce0b directly replaces the three * quantifiers with ?, enters v2.2.0 after v2.1.1, and its equivalent backport enters v1.8.9 after v1.8.8. AI attribution is decided only from the BIC object: its human author/committer identities and sole Signed-off-by trailer contain no AI marker. Therefore this is a real vulnerability with a human, non-AI-marked BIC: NOT_AI.
